title: Bar exam review II: constitutional law, criminal law and procedure, evidence and business associations
audience: a law graduate preparing for a U.S. bar exam (the Uniform Bar Exam or the NextGen bar exam)
prerequisites: L5, L6, U1, U2, U4; helpful: U5, U6.
purpose: Review the tested rules of constitutional law, criminal law and procedure, evidence and business associations, with family law, trusts and estates and the subjects tested only with supplied materials, and practice under time.
primary_reading: NCBE: exam information, content outlines and sample materials

weeks.1: Constitutional law review I: powers and federalism
weeks.2: Constitutional law review II: individual rights
weeks.5: Evidence review I: relevance, character and impeachment
weeks.6: Evidence review II: hearsay and privileges
weeks.8: Family law, trusts and estates review
weeks.9: Secured transactions and conflict of laws with supplied materials

blocks.deliverable: Write rule statements for 20 constitutional law issues.
Complete a timed 30-question criminal law and procedure set.
Week 7 midterm; complete a timed mixed set.
Answer two integrated question sets using supplied law.
Complete a timed mixed set and repair the three weakest topics.
Submit the project; take an unseen 180 minute final in week 14.

project: Timed practice exam: complete a 50-question mixed multiple-choice set assembled from this course's questions and NCBE's free sample questions, and a supplied integrated question set, under time; then write an error-log analysis and a repair plan.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
